findings.ref: tasks.md T-008 'Done When: Governance' vs Planned Files / implementation report 'Specification Differences' item 1
findings.note: T-008's own Done When bullet transcribes AC-032 as 'no path under plugins/** in either of this task's own commits', yet the same task's Planned Files explicitly authorize three new files under plugins/sdd-quality-loop/scripts/ (validate-resolver-evidence.{py,sh,ps1}, annotated agent-editable/direct-write, matching design.md's Components table and tasks.md Protected Files item 2). The implementation's disclosed reading (AC-032 is a REQ-007 registration-commit scope lock per acceptance-tests.md:74 and its design-content-review classification, not a per-task plugins ban) is the internally consistent one, and the deviation is disclosed rather than silently resolved -- but the tasks.md bullet itself is a sibling-task transcription defect the gate should confirm, as the report itself requests.

A matched Capability whose Registry conditional_facets[] is empty but whose Evidence entry omits the conditional_facet_evaluations key entirely passes validation: the schema's if/then forbids the key only on matched:false, and the positional check compares 0 recorded vs 0 declared. requirements.md Edge Cases states a matched Capability with empty declarations carries an explicit [] -- 'never an omitted key'. No semantically wrong content is admitted (both encodings represent zero facet evaluations), so this is a narrow structural-completeness gap, not a fail-open.

The --context override derives the affected-component set as set(projection.components.keys()) -- every component the Context declares, not the affected subset. This equals the dependency_pointers[]-derived ground truth only when every declared component is affected (as in the provenance-context-override-match fixture); a legitimate whole-repo projection for a subset-affected Feature would false-fire affected-component-provenance-mismatch. The failure direction is fail-closed (a refusal, never an acceptance), and design.md's own CLI sketch ('--context <resolved-context-projection-path>-derived equivalent') is itself ambiguous about the derivation, but the limitation deserves a note for the future caller-facing contract.

When canonicalize-sdd-yaml.py is absent beside the script, the loader falls back to invoking a bare 'canonicalize-sdd-yaml' from PATH. This is not a hand-rolled or lenient parser (still the canonicalizer contract, both declared input formats, fail-closed naming both attempts), but a PATH-resolved binary is outside the co-located-sibling shape every other dependency import in this validator uses (_import_sibling fails closed with dependency-unavailable), so the two dependency-resolution disciplines are inconsistent. Reachable only in a broken install; observation, not a spec violation with a demonstrated failure path.

findings.note: The AC-054 reader-side refusal is emitted as 'resolver-publication-in-progress', a thirteenth id outside the closed twelve-value enum. This follows Epic A4's precedent of operational refusal lines outside a validator's check-id enum, is disclosed in the report, and the driver's namespace-closure assertion whitelists exactly this one id -- recorded here as a labeling observation because design.md's Global Constraints describe the validator enum as closed at twelve without naming an operational-refusal id class (several other out-of-enum operational ids also exist in code: schema-discovery-failed, dependency-unavailable, registry-unreadable, canonicalizer-invocation-failed, argument-conflict; none has a firing fixture).
